nodes.summary: If `g, h` are continuous and `|g - h| ≤ ε` everywhere, then `|d_g(s, t) - d_h(s, t)| ≤ 4 ε` for all `s, t`. This is the estimate in the proof of Le Gall, *Random trees and applications*, Lemma 2.4: the correspondence `{(p_g(t), p_h(t))}` between `T_g` and `T_h` then has distortion at most `4 ‖g - h‖`, whence `d_GH(T_g, T_h) ≤ 2 ‖g - h‖`.
nodes.title: The coding is `4`-Lipschitz for the uniform norm

nodes.summary: If `|g - h| ≤ ε` everywhere, then `|m_g(s, t) - m_h(s, t)| ≤ ε` for all `s, t`.
nodes.title: Uniform continuity of the minimum in the coding function

nodes.summary: `ℝ` equipped with the pseudometric `d_g` coded by `g`; its metric quotient is the real tree `T_g` coded by `g` (Le Gall, *Random trees and applications*, Section 2.2).
nodes.title: The tree coded by a function

nodes.title: Distance in the coded tree

nodes.summary: For continuous `g`, the pseudometric space `(ℝ, d_g)` satisfies Gromov's four-point condition with constant `0`: `(x ∣ z)_w ≥ min ((x ∣ y)_w) ((y ∣ z)_w)` for all points, as every real tree does. Le Gall, *Random trees and applications*, Theorem 2.2, shows that the quotient `(T_g, d_g)` is a real tree; `0`-hyperbolicity is the metric half of that statement.
nodes.title: The tree coded by a continuous function is `0`-hyperbolic

nodes.summary: For `d_g`, `m_g(s, t) + m_g(t, u) ≤ g t + m_g(s, u)` because the larger of the two minima is at most `g t` and the smaller is at most `m_g(s, u)`, as `[s, u] ⊆ [s, t] ∪ [t, u]`.
nodes.title: Triangle inequality for the coded distance

nodes.summary: For `g : ℝ → ℝ`, `d_g(s, t) = g s + g t - 2 m_g(s, t)`, where `m_g(s, t)` is the minimum of `g` between `s` and `t`. For continuous `g` this is the pseudometric of the real tree coded by `g` (Le Gall, *Random trees and applications*, Section 2.2).
nodes.title: Distance coded by a function

nodes.summary: A larger interval has a smaller minimum.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of the minimum

nodes.summary: `m_g` is symmetric: the interval between `s` and `t` does not depend on their order.
nodes.title: Symmetry of the minimum

nodes.summary: For the minimum function `m_g`, for all `x, y, z, w`, `min (m_g(x, y) + m_g(z, w)) (m_g(y, z) + m_g(x, w)) ≤ m_g(x, z) + m_g(y, w)`. With `d_g = g + g - 2 m_g`, this is the four-point condition satisfied by the distance of a real tree (Le Gall, *Random trees and applications*, Theorem 2.2).
nodes.title: Four-point inequality for the minimum
